issues.description: The problem statement and UML describe a fully implemented Meal class (used throughout the exercise) but the template repository does not provide that class implementation. Instead, the template contains an Order.java class that has the same shape as the expected Meal class. This naming/placement mismatch between the problem statement (which refers to Meal) and the template (which provides Order) will confuse students and block straightforward implementation because they will not find the expected Meal class to use or extend.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide the Meal class in the template repository matching the problem statement (e.g., copy the implementation from the solution into src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java) and remove or rename the extraneous Order.java to avoid confusion. Ensure the template exposes a Meal class with constructors and getters as described so students see and use the intended type.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution refer to the core domain entity as 'Meal', but the template repository provides an 'Order' class that represents the same concept (name + ingredients). This inconsistent naming (Meal vs Order) across artifacts can confuse students about which class they should use and implement to satisfy the requirements.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier names across artifacts. Rename the template's Order class to Meal (file Order.java -> Meal.java, class Order -> Meal) or provide a Meal class in the template that mirrors the solution's Meal API and remove/rename the Order class so that the problem statement, template, and solution consistently use the same name 'Meal'.
